A.explanation: This is $Q/E$, the fraction of input energy that is wasted, not the fraction that is useful.

B.explanation: This gives $(Q/E) - 1$, which is negative since $Q < E$ and so cannot be an efficiency.

C.explanation: Useful output is $E - Q$, so efficiency is $(E-Q)/E = 1 - Q/E$.

D.explanation: This subtracts energy $Q$ from the pure number $1$, which is physically inconsistent and does not equal $(E-Q)/E$.

hints: Notice the input to the motor is total energy $E$ and the wasted part is $Q$, so the useful output must be $E - Q$.
Recall efficiency is defined as useful output divided by total input, so write $(E - Q)/E$.
Split the fraction $(E-Q)/E$ into $E/E - Q/E$ and simplify to match one of the given forms.
walkthrough: Identify the energies: total supplied energy is $E$ and wasted energy is $Q$, so by conservation of energy the useful work is $E - Q$.
State the rule for efficiency: $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output} / \text{total input}$.
Rearrange by dividing each term: $(E-Q)/E = E/E - Q/E = 1 - (Q/E)$.
This matches the form $1 - (Q/E)$. This is option C.
